research.topic: storage-deploy: Info.plist keys, free-Apple-ID sideloading limits, local storage layout and serialization, memory budget, background processing, XcodeGen/Swift 6 build settings for the Mapper iOS 18 LiDAR app (verified against Apple doc JSON on 2026-09-28)

facts.claim: UIRequiredDeviceCapabilities has NO value for LiDAR. The complete value list is: accelerometer, arkit, armv7, arm64, auto-focus-camera, bluetooth-le, camera-flash, driverkit, front-facing-camera, gamekit, gps, gyroscope, healthkit, iphone-performance-gaming-tier, iphone-ipad-minimum-performance-a12, location-services, magnetometer, metal, microphone, nfc, opengles-1/2/3, peer-peer, sms, still-camera, telephony, video-camera, wifi. Use `arkit` (and optionally `metal`, `arm64`) and gate LiDAR at runtime with RoomCaptureSession.isSupported / ARWorldTrackingConfiguration.supportsSceneReconstruction(.mesh).
facts.api: Info.plist: <key>UIRequiredDeviceCapabilities</key><array><string>arkit</string><string>arm64</string><string>metal</string></array>
facts.notes: Apple: 'Specify only the features that your app absolutely requires.' The key only matters for App Store install gating; a sideloaded IPA installs regardless, so it is documentation, not enforcement. Dictionary form with true/false values is also allowed.

facts.claim: RoomPlan, ARKit scene reconstruction and RealityKit Object Capture require NO entitlement on iOS. The Entitlements reference lists ARKit entitlements only under 'Enterprise' for visionOS (com.apple.developer.arkit.main-camera-access.allow etc.). The only requirement is NSCameraUsageDescription in Info.plist; the app crashes on first camera access without it.
facts.api: Info.plist: <key>NSCameraUsageDescription</key><string>Mapper uses the camera and LiDAR to scan rooms and objects.</string>
facts.notes: Apple doc: 'This key is required if your app uses APIs that access the device's camera.' RoomCaptureSession.isSupported doc: 'This property is true if the device contains a LiDAR Scanner.' No Metal capability key is needed to use Metal.

facts.claim: On iOS, PhotogrammetrySession supports ONLY the .reduced detail level. .preview/.medium/.full/.raw are macOS 12+/Mac Catalyst 15+ only and .custom (CustomDetailSpecification, maximumPolygonCount, texture dims) is macOS 14+ only. .reduced = <50k triangles, ~10 MB, diffuse + AO + normal maps.
facts.api:
enum Detail { case reduced /* iOS 17+ */; case preview, medium, full, raw /* macOS only */; case custom /* macOS 14+ */ }
case modelFile(url: URL, detail: PhotogrammetrySession.Request.Detail = .reduced, geometry: PhotogrammetrySession.Request.Geometry? = nil)
case pointCloud
case poses
case bounds
facts.availability: PhotogrammetrySession iOS 17.0+; .reduced iOS 17.0+; other detail cases macOS only
facts.notes: Doc text: 'On iOS, only one detail level – .reduced – is currently supported.' So the 'textured realistic model' output for objects on device is capped at ~50k triangles. Requesting a macOS-only case in code that compiles for iOS will fail with an availability error (the cases carry macOS-only availability).

facts.claim: SceneKit is deprecated in the iOS 26 SDK: the SceneKit framework, SCNView, SCNScene and ARKit's ARSCNView are all marked deprecated at iOS 26.0 ('Use RealityView instead' / 'SceneKit is deprecated, use RealityKit instead', WWDC25 session 288). They still compile with Xcode 26.6 (warnings only). Model I/O (MDLAsset, MDLMesh, MDLAsset.export(to:), canExportFileExtension(_:)) is NOT deprecated. RealityKit ARView and ModelEntity are not deprecated.
facts.api:
class ARSCNView /* deprecated iOS 26.0 */
class SCNView, class SCNScene /* deprecated iOS 26.0 */
class MDLAsset { func export(to URL: URL) throws; class func canExportFileExtension(_ extension: String) -> Bool } /* iOS 9.0+, not deprecated */
facts.availability: SceneKit deprecated iOS 26.0; Model I/O iOS 9.0+; RealityKit ARView iOS 13.0+
facts.notes: Xcode 26 release notes: 'SceneKit is now deprecated across all Apple platforms... For new projects, Apple recommends using RealityKit.' Architecture choice: render with RealityKit (RealityView/ARView) or a custom Metal renderer; keep Model I/O only for OBJ/USD export. Deprecation warnings do not fail the CI build unless warnings-as-errors is enabled.

facts.claim: simd_float4x4 is NOT Codable. Its documented conformances are exactly: BitwiseCopyable, Copyable, CustomDebugStringConvertible, Equatable, Escapable, Sendable. A wrapper is required for JSON (e.g. encode columns.0...columns.3 as [Float] of 16 values, column-major) or store poses in a binary blob. simd_float3x3 (ARCamera.intrinsics) likewise needs a wrapper.
facts.api:
struct simd_float4x4 // conforms to BitwiseCopyable, Copyable, CustomDebugStringConvertible, Equatable, Escapable, Sendable
var transform: simd_float4x4 { get } // ARCamera, ARAnchor
var intrinsics: simd_float3x3 { get } // ARCamera
facts.availability: simd all iOS versions; ARCamera.transform/intrinsics iOS 11.0+
facts.notes: Because it is BitwiseCopyable you can also write it raw: `withUnsafeBytes(of: m) { Data($0) }` (64 bytes, 16-byte aligned columns) and read back with `data.withUnsafeBytes { $0.loadUnaligned(as: simd_float4x4.self) }` (loadUnaligned is available in Swift 5.7+; Xcode 16 notes mention a false deprecation warning that was fixed).

facts.claim: Long-running processing cannot be continued in the background on iOS 18. BGContinuedProcessingTask / BGContinuedProcessingTaskRequest (start in foreground, continue in background with a Live Activity) are iOS 26.0+ only. On iOS 18 the options are: (a) beginBackgroundTask(withName:expirationHandler:) which gives 'a limited amount of time' (community: ~30 s) and (b) BGProcessingTask which 'run[s] only when the device is idle' and 'The system terminates any background processing tasks running when the user starts using the device' (needs UIBackgroundModes=processing + BGTaskSchedulerPermittedIdentifiers, registration must complete before applicationDidFinishLaunching ends). Therefore mesh/photogrammetry processing must run while the app is foregrounded; keep the screen awake with UIApplication.shared.isIdleTimerDisabled = true.
facts.availability: BGProcessingTask iOS 13.0+; BGContinuedProcessingTask iOS 26.0+; beginBackgroundTask iOS 7.0+
facts.notes: Info.plist keys: UIBackgroundModes value 'processing' (iOS 4.0+), BGTaskSchedulerPermittedIdentifiers array of strings (iOS 13.0+). 'Register each task identifier only once. The system kills the app on the second registration.' On the future iOS 26 device you can adopt BGContinuedProcessingTask behind #available(iOS 26, *); GPU use in background needs entitlement com.apple.developer.background-tasks.continued-processing.gpu, which a free team profile will not carry.

facts.claim: Swift 6 language mode is opt-in via SWIFT_VERSION=6 (-swift-version 6). XcodeGen's base setting preset hardcodes SWIFT_VERSION: '5.0' for every generated project, so a project.yml that does not override it compiles in Swift 5 mode with minimal concurrency checking: Sendable/actor-isolation problems are at most warnings and will not fail the CI build. Xcode 26 changes only affect NEW Xcode templates (Default Actor Isolation = MainActor); XcodeGen projects get the 'existing project' defaults (SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION unset = nonisolated, SWIFT_APPROACHABLE_CONCURRENCY unset = NO).
facts.api:
project.yml:
options:
  deploymentTarget:
    iOS: "18.0"
targets:
  Mapper:
    type: application
    platform: iOS
    settings:
      base:
        SWIFT_VERSION: "5.0"          # keep Swift 5 mode; do NOT set 6
        SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY: minimal  # or targeted; 'complete' only adds warnings in 5 mode
        TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY: "1"
        IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET: "18.0"
        CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED: "NO"
facts.notes: Verified in XcodeGen SettingPresets/base.yml (SWIFT_VERSION: '5.0') and Platforms/iOS.yml (SDKROOT: iphoneos, TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY: '1,2', LD_RUNPATH_SEARCH_PATHS). Apple build-settings reference: SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY 'is always complete when in the Swift 6 language mode and produces errors instead of warnings'; SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION 'When set to MainActor, @MainActor isolation will be inferred by default'; SWIFT_APPROACHABLE_CONCURRENCY enables DisableOutwardActorInference, GlobalActorIsolatedTypesUsability, InferIsolatedConformances, InferSendableFromCaptures, NonisolatedNonsendingByDefault. Xcode 16 release notes: 'The SWIFT_VERSION build setting now allows building with the Swift 6 language mode... You can enable the Swift 6 language mode using the -swift-version 6 compiler flag.' ENABLE_PREVIEWS is not needed for a CI/xcodebuild build.

facts.claim: Free Apple ID sideloading limits (Sideloadly FAQ): 'a free Apple Developer account is limited to 3 sideloaded apps' installed at once; 'only allows the app to function for 7 days' then re-sideload with the same Apple ID; 'You may create up to 10 App IDs every 7 days'; 'Since iOS 16+, Apple now requires users to enable Developer Mode'. Developer Mode is a per-device switch (Settings > Privacy & Security > Developer Mode, requires restart) and the toggle only appears after the device has been paired/had an install attempted.
facts.notes: Apple: 'Developer Mode only appears in Settings if you initiate pairing or if you previously paired the device'; 'To run your iOS... app that you install from an iOS Package Archive, enable Developer Mode on that device.' Device count: community sources (Corellium) say free accounts are limited to 3 unique device UDIDs per rolling 7 days; Sideloadly FAQ does not state a device limit. Using one free Apple ID on two iPhones (13 Pro Max + the iOS 26 phone) is fine within that limit. Note Sideloadly rewrites the bundle id to <id>.<TEAMID> (observed in this repo's earlier app: com.shreehub.interpreter.24THSTQU78); custom UTIs and BGTask identifiers are independent strings and unaffected, but anything keyed on Bundle.main.bundleIdentifier must not assume the plain id. 10 App IDs/week includes each bundle id; re-installing the same bundle id does not consume a new App ID.

facts.claim: NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription is required only if the app writes to the Photos library (PHPhotoLibrary add-only). Not needed for saving into the app's own Documents or for share sheets. If the app also reads Photos, NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription is required instead.
facts.api: Info.plist: <key>NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription</key><string>Mapper saves rendered snapshots to your photo library.</string>
facts.notes: Doc: 'This key is required if your app uses APIs that have write access to the user's photo library.' Exporting via UIActivityViewController / ShareLink does not need it.

facts.claim: To expose Documents/ in the Files app under 'On My iPhone' set both UIFileSharingEnabled=YES and LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace=YES. UIFileSharingEnabled: 'If you set this key to YES, your app can share files with the user. Place the files in a Documents folder... The default value is NO.' Alternative single key: UISupportsDocumentBrowser=YES ('To allow other apps to open and edit the files stored in your app's Documents folder').
facts.api:
Info.plist:
<key>UIFileSharingEnabled</key><true/>
<key>LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace</key><true/>
facts.availability: UIFileSharingEnabled iOS 3.2+; LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace iOS 2.0+ (doc listing); UISupportsDocumentBrowser iOS 11.0+
facts.notes: The 'both keys' requirement for On My iPhone visibility is community-verified (multiple blogs, Apple forums), the individual key semantics are from Apple docs. Consequence: everything under Documents/ becomes user-visible and user-deletable via Files and Finder/iTunes, and Documents is backed up by default. Keep raw scan buffers under Documents/Projects/<uuid>/raw but mark them isExcludedFromBackup, or put regenerable caches in Library/Caches.

facts.claim: A custom package document type (.mapperproj as a directory package) is declared with CFBundleDocumentTypes + UTExportedTypeDeclarations. The exported UTI must conform to com.apple.package (a directory shown as a single file) and should also conform to public.content; use the reverse-DNS identifier (letters, digits, hyphen, period only; never prefix public/dyn/com.apple), and list the extension under UTTypeTagSpecification/public.filename-extension. Document-type keys: CFBundleTypeName, CFBundleTypeRole (Editor/Viewer/Shell/QLGenerator/None), LSHandlerRank (Owner/Default/Alternate/None), LSItemContentTypes (array of UTIs), LSTypeIsPackage (bool).
facts.api:
<key>UTExportedTypeDeclarations</key>
<array><dict>
  <key>UTTypeIdentifier</key><string>com.shreehub.mapper.project</string>
  <key>UTTypeConformsTo</key><array><string>com.apple.package</string><string>public.content</string></array>
  <key>UTTypeDescription</key><string>Mapper Project</string>
  <key>UTTypeTagSpecification</key><dict><key>public.filename-extension</key><array><string>mapperproj</string></array></dict>
</dict></array>
<key>CFBundleDocumentTypes</key>
<array><dict>
  <key>CFBundleTypeName</key><string>Mapper Project</string>
  <key>CFBundleTypeRole</key><string>Editor</string>
  <key>LSHandlerRank</key><string>Owner</string>
  <key>LSTypeIsPackage</key><true/>
  <key>LSItemContentTypes</key><array><string>com.shreehub.mapper.project</string></array>
</dict></array>

// Swift side
static var package: UTType { get }            // com.apple.package
init(exportedAs identifier: String, conformingTo parentType: UTType? = nil)
init(importedAs identifier: String, conformingTo parentType: UTType? = nil)
static var usdz: UTType { get }; static var pdf: UTType { get }; static var json: UTType { get }; static var heic: UTType { get }; static var jpeg: UTType { get }; static var png: UTType { get }
facts.availability: CFBundleDocumentTypes iOS 2.0+; UTExportedTypeDeclarations iOS 5.0+; UTType iOS 14.0+
facts.notes: Apple: 'make sure that it conforms to public.data or com.apple.package to ensure the Finder or Files app can represent it... For document types, conform to public.content'. Use UTImportedTypeDeclarations only for types owned by someone else (e.g. if you wanted .obj: public.geometry-definition-format already exists in the system so don't redeclare it). Package UTIs are only respected when the extension is on a directory; a zip-based single file should instead conform to public.data (and public.zip-archive).

facts.claim: UISupportedInterfaceOrientations takes UIInterfaceOrientationPortrait, UIInterfaceOrientationPortraitUpsideDown (ignored on devices without a Home button), UIInterfaceOrientationLandscapeLeft, UIInterfaceOrientationLandscapeRight. iPad-specific override key is UISupportedInterfaceOrientations~ipad. With GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE the same is settable via INFOPLIST_KEY_UISupportedInterfaceOrientations / INFOPLIST_KEY_UISupportedInterfaceOrientations_iPhone.
facts.api: <key>UISupportedInterfaceOrientations</key><array><string>UIInterfaceOrientationPortrait</string></array>
facts.notes: For an AR scanning app restrict to portrait; ARKit camera transforms are independent of UI orientation but a fixed orientation simplifies keyframe/intrinsics bookkeeping (ARCamera.imageResolution is landscape 1920x1440 regardless).

facts.claim: Other Info.plist keys worth setting: UILaunchScreen (dictionary, may be empty {}, iOS 14+, no storyboard needed), UIApplicationSceneManifest (iOS 13+, optional for SwiftUI App lifecycle), ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption=NO (App Store Connect only, harmless), NSSupportsLiveActivities (iOS 16.1+, only for the iOS 26 BGContinuedProcessingTask path). Not needed: NSMotionUsageDescription (ARKit does not require it), NSMicrophoneUsageDescription (unless audio is captured), NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription.
facts.api:
<key>UILaunchScreen</key><dict/>
<key>ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption</key><false/>
facts.notes: NSMotionUsageDescription doc lists CMSensorRecorder/CMPedometer/CMMotionActivityManager/CMMovementDisorderManager as the triggering APIs; ARKit's internal IMU use does not prompt. Privacy manifest (PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy) is enforced only at App Store submission, not for sideloaded IPAs.

facts.claim: RoomPlan device gate and session API: RoomCaptureSession.isSupported is 'true if the device contains a LiDAR Scanner'. Custom-UI flow: create RoomCaptureSession(arSession:) (iOS 17+) sharing your own ARSession so the same session can run scene reconstruction and grab ARFrames, run(configuration:), delegate receives captureSession(_:didUpdate:) with a CapturedRoom and captureSession(_:didEndWith:error:) with CapturedRoomData, then RoomBuilder.capturedRoom(from:) async. CapturedRoomData and CapturedStructure are Codable (Encodable+Decodable, Sendable) so raw scan data can be persisted as JSON/plist and re-processed later; CapturedRoom has encode(to:)/init(from:) too.
facts.availability: RoomPlan iOS 16.0+; init(arSession:), stop(pauseARSession:), StructureBuilder, export(to:metadataURL:...) iOS 17.0+
facts.notes: export writes USD/USDZ; 'Before iOS 17.4, the first letter of the USD file name needs to be a character other than a number' (irrelevant on iOS 18 but keep names alphabetic anyway). CapturedRoom.Error.deviceNotSupported exists for export on unsupported devices.

facts.claim: Object Capture on iOS requires 'iPhone or iPad with a LiDAR Scanner and an A14 Bionic chip or later' (iPhone 12 Pro and newer); iPhone 13 Pro Max (A15) qualifies. Gate with ObjectCaptureSession.isSupported (@MainActor) and PhotogrammetrySession.isSupported. ObjectCaptureSession is a @MainActor class; start(imagesDirectory:configuration:) requires an EMPTY writable directory (created if missing) and an optional empty checkpointDirectory; maximumNumberOfInputImages caps on-device capture unless isOverCaptureEnabled (then extras are skipped for on-device reconstruction).
facts.notes: checkpointDirectory doc: on iOS, passing the same checkpointDirectory used by the ObjectCaptureSession (or an interrupted PhotogrammetrySession) lets reconstruction resume instead of starting from scratch; 'Ensure that each checkpointDirectory is unique for each images folder.' Layout suggestion: Documents/Projects/<uuid>/raw/objects/<objId>/Images and .../Snapshots (checkpoint). Limits.maximumNumberOfInputImages is device-specific and not documented numerically; read PhotogrammetrySession.limits at runtime. Sample images exceeding the limit produce .invalidSample outputs and are ignored. PhotogrammetrySample lets you feed your own keyframes + LiDAR depth (depthDataMap) + gravity, which is how you can build a textured room model from ARKit keyframes without ObjectCaptureSession, subject to the input-image cap and .reduced output.

facts.claim: ARKit mesh/depth/pose data needed for the raw/ store, with exact accessors: ARMeshAnchor.geometry (ARMeshGeometry) exposes vertices/normals (ARGeometrySource: MTLBuffer + format/stride/offset/count/componentsPerVector), faces (ARGeometryElement: MTLBuffer, bytesPerIndex, indexCountPerPrimitive, count) and optional classification. ARFrame gives sceneDepth/smoothedSceneDepth (ARDepthData.depthMap Float32 'fdep' CVPixelBuffer + confidenceMap 8-bit 'L008'), capturedImage (CVPixelBuffer, 420 bi-planar), camera.transform (simd_float4x4), camera.intrinsics (simd_float3x3), camera.imageResolution. ARMeshAnchor is NSSecureCoding + Sendable; ARAnchor.transform and .identifier are per-chunk keys.
facts.availability: Mesh APIs iOS 13.4+; sceneDepth/ARDepthData iOS 14.0+; ARCamera iOS 11.0+
facts.notes: Copy mesh chunks off the MTLBuffer immediately in the delegate: Data(bytes: source.buffer.contents() + source.offset, count: source.count * source.stride). Vertices are float3 packed at stride 12 (verify at runtime via .format == .float3 / stride), faces uint32 x 3 (bytesPerIndex 4, indexCountPerPrimitive 3), classification uint8 per face. Depth resolution is 256x192 Float32 (community-verified; not in doc JSON) = 196,608 bytes per frame raw; storing as Float16 halves it (98 KB) and 16-bit PNG via CIContext L16 gives ~100-150 KB.

facts.claim: ARWorldMap is NSSecureCoding; persist with NSKeyedArchiver.archivedData(withRootObject:requiringSecureCoding: true) and restore with NSKeyedUnarchiver.unarchivedObject(ofClass: ARWorldMap.self, from:), then set ARWorldTrackingConfiguration.initialWorldMap. Obtain it with getCurrentWorldMap(completionHandler:) or the async currentWorldMap(). ARKit calls the completion on the session's delegateQueue (main queue if nil); do the archiving on another queue.
facts.api:
class ARWorldMap // NSSecureCoding, NSCopying
func getCurrentWorldMap(completionHandler: @escaping @Sendable (ARWorldMap?, (any Error)?) -> Void)
func currentWorldMap() async throws -> ARWorldMap
var initialWorldMap: ARWorldMap? { get set } // ARWorldTrackingConfiguration
var anchors: [ARAnchor] { get set }; var rawFeaturePoints: ARPointCloud { get } // ARWorldMap
class func archivedData(withRootObject object: Any, requiringSecureCoding requiresSecureCoding: Bool) throws -> Data
@nonobjc static func unarchivedObject<DecodedObjectType>(ofClass cls: DecodedObjectType.Type, from data: Data) throws -> DecodedObjectType? where DecodedObjectType : NSObject, DecodedObjectType : NSCoding
facts.availability: ARWorldMap iOS 12.0+; NSKeyedArchiver secure APIs iOS 11.0+
facts.notes: Apple's own sample in the ARWorldMap doc: `let data = try NSKeyedArchiver.archivedData(withRootObject: worldMap, requiringSecureCoding: true); try data.write(to: url)`. ARMeshAnchors in the map's anchors array bloat the archive; consider stripping them (map.anchors is settable) and keeping mesh chunks in your own binary files. Size is typically a few MB to tens of MB for a room.

facts.claim: ARSession delegate threading: 'If this value [delegateQueue] is nil (the default), the session calls your delegate methods on the main queue.' ARSessionDelegate (extends ARSessionObserver) has optional session(_:didUpdate: ARFrame), session(_:didAdd:), session(_:didUpdate: [ARAnchor]), session(_:didRemove:). Set delegateQueue to a serial background queue for mesh/depth extraction so the UI is not blocked; ARFrame and CVPixelBuffer are not Sendable, so copy out Data/simd values inside the callback and hop to the main actor with only value types. Never retain ARFrames: ARKit warns when a delegate retains more than ~10 frames and the camera starts dropping frames at ~15-20 retained (frozen viewfinder).
facts.notes: Concurrency implication: in Swift 5 mode (the XcodeGen default) a plain `final class ARDelegate: NSObject, ARSessionDelegate` compiles with no isolation complaints. Do NOT mark the delegate class @MainActor if delegateQueue is a background queue (runtime isolation assertions in Swift 6.2 can trap) and do not set SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION=MainActor for the module, otherwise conformances to the nonisolated ObjC protocol produce errors/warnings ('main actor-isolated instance method cannot satisfy nonisolated requirement'). Apple forum thread 765644 ('ARKit delegate code broken by Swift 6') documents this class of failure; the fix is nonisolated delegate methods that forward Sendable copies. ARFrame retention numbers are from Apple forum 695404 (community/Apple engineer), not the doc JSON.

facts.claim: Backup exclusion: URLResourceValues.isExcludedFromBackup (Bool?, get set) / URLResourceKey.isExcludedFromBackupKey. Apple warns: 'Some operations commonly made to user documents will cause this property to be reset to false and so this property should not be used on user documents' and 'Set this property each time you save a file'. Set it on the raw/ directory of each project after every write batch (excluding a directory excludes its contents). Files in Library/Caches are never backed up and can be purged by the system under storage pressure; use it only for regenerable intermediates (photogrammetry checkpoints, thumbnails).
facts.availability: isExcludedFromBackup iOS 8.0+ (key iOS 5.1+); volumeAvailableCapacity keys iOS 11.0+
facts.notes: Check free space before a scan with `try FileManager.default.url(for: .documentDirectory, ...).resourceValues(forKeys: [.volumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsageKey])`. A 5-minute room scan budget (see estimate fact) is ~200-350 MB, so refuse to start below ~1 GB free.

facts.claim: iOS data protection default for app files is 'Complete until first user authentication' (NSFileProtectionCompleteUntilFirstUserAuthentication): files stay readable after the first unlock even when the device is later locked, so background/locked-screen access is not blocked by file protection. Change with Data.write(to:options: .completeFileProtection) or URLFileProtection via setResourceValue(_:forKey: .fileProtectionKey). No Info.plist key is needed for the default.
facts.api:
struct URLFileProtection { static let none, complete, completeUnlessOpen, completeUntilFirstUserAuthentication, completeWhenUserInactive }
var fileProtection: URLFileProtection? { get } // URLResourceValues
static let protectionKey: FileAttributeKey
func setAttributes(_ attributes: [FileAttributeKey : Any], ofItemAtPath path: String) throws
facts.notes: Leave the default. Do not use .complete on scan data or a locked-screen write from an expiring background task fails.

facts.claim: Binary buffer storage: Data(bytes:count:) copies, Data(bytesNoCopy:count:deallocator:) wraps, withUnsafeBytes gives a raw pointer; for simd types keep 16-byte column alignment by writing raw simd_float4x4 (64 B) / simd_float3 as float3 (16 B stride, NOT 12) or explicitly pack Float components. Prefer a small header (magic, version, count, stride) + raw arrays per chunk file; JSON for project.json (Codable) and poses (wrapper types). Binary plist and SQLite are unnecessary for this scale (hundreds of files, tens of MB); Codable JSON + raw binary blobs is the simplest robust choice.
facts.notes: Swift's SIMD3<Float>/simd_float3 has stride 16 and size 16 in memory; ARKit's vertex buffer is packed float3 at stride 12. When converting, use MemoryLayout<T>.stride in headers and never assume. Loading raw bytes with loadUnaligned avoids alignment traps when a header offset is not a multiple of 16.

facts.claim: Image encoding without third-party code: CIContext.writeHEIFRepresentation / writeJPEGRepresentation / writePNGRepresentation take a CIImage (create with CIImage(cvPixelBuffer:)) and write directly to a URL; CIFormat.L16 is a 16-bit single-channel format usable for 16-bit PNG depth, .Lh (half float) / .Lf (float) for single-channel float; kCGImageDestinationLossyCompressionQuality controls HEIC/JPEG quality via options [.init(rawValue: kCGImageDestinationLossyCompressionQuality as String): 0.8]. AVFileType.heic / .jpg exist for AVCapturePhoto paths.
facts.api:
func writeHEIFRepresentation(of image: CIImage, to url: URL, format: CIFormat, colorSpace: CGColorSpace, options: [CIImageRepresentationOption : Any] = [:]) throws // iOS 11+
func writeJPEGRepresentation(of image: CIImage, to url: URL, colorSpace: CGColorSpace, options: [CIImageRepresentationOption : Any] = [:]) throws // iOS 10+
func writePNGRepresentation(of image: CIImage, to url: URL, format: CIFormat, colorSpace: CGColorSpace, options: [CIImageRepresentationOption : Any] = [:]) throws // iOS 11+
func heifRepresentation(of image: CIImage, format: CIFormat, colorSpace: CGColorSpace, options: [CIImageRepresentationOption : Any] = [:]) -> Data?
static let L16: CIFormat; static let Lh: CIFormat; static let Lf: CIFormat; static let RGBA16: CIFormat
let kCGImageDestinationLossyCompressionQuality: CFString
static let heic: AVFileType; static let jpg: AVFileType
facts.availability: CoreImage writers iOS 10/11+; CIFormat L16/Lh/Lf iOS 10.0+
facts.notes: For depth, converting Float32 metres to UInt16 millimetres yourself and writing a 16-bit grayscale PNG via CGImageDestination (ImageIO) is more predictable than CIContext's float-to-L16 conversion; raw Float16 files (98 KB) are simplest and fastest if the data never leaves the app. HEIC encode of a 1920x1440 keyframe on A15 is ~20-40 ms (community range) and yields ~300-500 KB; JPEG q0.8 ~600-900 KB.

facts.claim: Memory budget: iPhone 13 Pro Max has 6 GB RAM (ProcessInfo.processInfo.physicalMemory). The per-app jetsam 'ActiveHardMemoryLimit' is device-specific and undocumented; community reports for 4 GB iPhone 13 show os_proc_available_memory() ~2.2-2.3 GB at launch, so ~3-3.3 GB is the plausible ceiling on the 6 GB Pro Max (unsure). Apple's guidance: call os_proc_available_memory() (returns bytes available before the limit, 0 if already over) and treat it as advisory; the com.apple.developer.kernel.increased-memory-limit entitlement (iOS 15+) raises it 'on some device models' but requires the entitlement in the provisioning profile, which a free-team Sideloadly profile will not include (unsure).
facts.api:
extern size_t os_proc_available_memory(); // import os; Swift: let bytes = os_proc_available_memory()
var physicalMemory: UInt64 { get } // ProcessInfo
var recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize: UInt64 { get } // MTLDevice, iOS 16+
var currentAllocatedSize: Int { get } // MTLDevice
nonisolated class let didReceiveMemoryWarningNotification: NSNotification.Name // UIApplication
var thermalState: ProcessInfo.ThermalState { get }; enum ThermalState { case nominal, fair, serious, critical }
var isLowPowerModeEnabled: Bool { get }
facts.availability: os_proc_available_memory iOS 13.0+; increased-memory-limit entitlement iOS 15.0+; recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize iOS 16.0+
facts.notes: Log os_proc_available_memory() at launch and during scanning on the real device in build 1; design for a working set under ~1.5 GB: stream mesh chunks to disk as anchors update (keep only latest per anchor id in RAM), write keyframes/depth immediately, never hold ARFrames, feed PhotogrammetrySession from a directory URL (not an in-memory PhotogrammetrySample array), and downsample keyframes (1920x1440 -> 1440x1080) if the photogrammetry step trips memory warnings. The MTLDevice.recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize value on iOS is the GPU-visible budget (unified memory); check it before allocating large Metal buffers.

facts.claim: Storage estimate for a 5-minute room scan at ~1 keyframe/s (300 keyframes): keyframes HEIC ~300-500 KB each = 90-150 MB (JPEG q0.8 would be ~180-270 MB); depth 256x192 Float16 raw = 98 KB (16-bit PNG ~100-150 KB) x300 = 30-45 MB; confidence 49 KB x300 = 15 MB (or pack into the depth file); poses JSON ~200 B/frame = <1 MB; final ARKit mesh of a 20-40 m2 room ~200k-500k vertices and ~0.5-1M triangles = (vertices 12 B + normals 12 B) x N + faces 12 B x F + classification 1 B x F = 15-40 MB, or 2-3x that if per-anchor history snapshots are kept; ARWorldMap 5-30 MB; derived textured USDZ (.reduced) ~10 MB + clean model + PDF ~2 MB. Total ~200-350 MB per room, so a 20-room building is several GB: keep raw/ excluded from backup and offer 'delete raw data' after derived outputs exist.
facts.notes: Sizes per element are computed from verified formats (float3 vertices, uint32 triangle indices, 256x192 Float32 depth, .reduced ~10 MB per Apple's table). Keyframe HEIC sizes are typical community numbers for 1920x1440 photos, not Apple-documented.

facts.claim: ARKit ARFrame camera image on iPhone 13 Pro Max default world-tracking video format is 1920x1440 (ARCamera.imageResolution), 60 fps; ARWorldTrackingConfiguration.supportedVideoFormats also offers 3840x2160 (4K) on A15+ from iOS 16 (ARKit 6) which quadruples keyframe size and memory pressure; stay on the default for scanning.
facts.api:
var imageResolution: CGSize { get } // ARCamera
var videoFormat: ARConfiguration.VideoFormat { get set }
facts.notes: The 4K availability is from the WWDC22 'Discover ARKit 6' session; the exact per-device format list must be read from ARWorldTrackingConfiguration.supportedVideoFormats at runtime.

facts.notes: Verified in ProjectSpec.md (info.path/properties, entitlements.path/properties, settings.base, deploymentTarget forms). GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE + INFOPLIST_KEY_* is an alternative but XcodeGen's `info` block is simpler for the document-type dictionaries. Do not add `entitlements` with increased-memory-limit or background GPU keys: an unsigned build ignores them and Sideloadly's free profile cannot grant them, and a mismatch between the binary's entitlements and the profile makes the install fail.

facts.claim: CapturedRoom.USDExportOptions: .parametric (editable primitives, Boolean ops), .mesh (polygonal walls with openings cut out, recessed areas), .model (like mesh plus ModelProvider 3D models for recognised objects). All three produce USD/USDZ. For the 'clean architectural model' output use .parametric or .mesh; for the floor plan derive from CapturedRoom.walls/doors/windows/openings/floors (each a CapturedRoom.Surface with transform + dimensions).
facts.notes: Doc table: Parametric supports 'Changing the size or position of objects, windows, or doors' and 'Boolean operations'; Mesh/Model support 'Polygonal walls' and 'Windows, doors, and other openings cut out of wall geometry'.

gotchas: Do not set SWIFT_VERSION to 6 or SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION=MainActor in project.yml: ARSessionDelegate / RoomCaptureSessionDelegate callbacks arrive on a dispatch queue with non-Sendable ARFrame/CVPixelBuffer/ARMeshAnchor payloads and the build would fail on isolation errors that cannot be verified locally. Stay in Swift 5 mode with SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY=minimal or targeted; add @MainActor only on SwiftUI views / observable models and pass Sendable value copies out of delegate methods with Task { @MainActor in }.

ObjectCaptureSession is a @MainActor class; every call to it (start, startDetecting, finish, reading state) must happen on the main actor. PhotogrammetrySession is not @MainActor and its outputs is an AsyncSequence you iterate in a Task; keep the Task alive (store it) or the session is cancelled.

ObjectCaptureSession.start(imagesDirectory:configuration:) and PhotogrammetrySession checkpointDirectory require EMPTY directories, otherwise the session goes to .failed; create a fresh UUID-named directory per capture and never reuse an images folder with a different checkpoint folder.
Apple's iOS Object Capture output is fixed at .reduced (<50k triangles, ~10 MB). Do not plan on .medium/.full on device; the compiler will reject those cases for iOS deployment.

isExcludedFromBackup silently resets to false after common file operations (e.g. atomic replace of a directory). Re-apply it on the raw/ directory after each save and verify with resourceValues(forKeys: [.isExcludedFromBackupKey]) in a debug log.

UIFileSharingEnabled + LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace makes every file under Documents visible in Files, including partially written mesh chunks. Write into a temp file in the same directory and rename (FileManager.replaceItemAt / moveItem) so users and the Files indexer never see half files; or keep in-progress scans under Library/Application Support and move the finished package into Documents.

SceneKit/ARSCNView are deprecated in the iOS 26 SDK: they compile with warnings but Apple ships no fixes. If any teammate's plan used ARSCNView for the live mesh preview, switch to RealityKit (ARView with .showSceneUnderstanding debug option, or a RealityView) or a Metal MTKView.

Never hold an ARFrame beyond the delegate callback (copy pixel buffers / poses out first). ARKit logs 'ARSessionDelegate is retaining N ARFrames' at >10 and the camera feed freezes at ~15-20 retained frames.

BGProcessingTask is useless for the user-facing pipeline on iOS 18: it only runs when the device is idle and is killed the moment the user touches the phone. Run processing in the foreground with isIdleTimerDisabled = true and a progress UI; adopt BGContinuedProcessingTask only behind #available(iOS 26, *).

Sideloadly changes the bundle id to <bundleId>.<TEAMID>. Anything that hardcodes 'com.shreehub.mapper' (BGTask identifiers are free strings so fine; UTIs are fine; but Bundle.main.bundleIdentifier comparisons, app-group names, keychain access groups are not) must not assume the original id. Entitlements that need a paid team (increased-memory-limit, background GPU, app groups) are silently unavailable.

Free Apple ID: only 3 sideloaded apps per device at once (Interpreter + Mapper + one more), 10 new App IDs per rolling 7 days, apps stop launching after 7 days. Re-sideload weekly; keep the same bundle id so the app container (Documents/Projects) survives reinstall.
Developer Mode must be enabled separately on each iPhone (13 Pro Max and later the iOS 26 phone); the toggle is hidden until a pairing/install attempt, and enabling it reboots the device.
recommendations: Info.plist (via XcodeGen `info.properties`): NSCameraUsageDescription; UIRequiredDeviceCapabilities [arkit, arm64, metal]; UIFileSharingEnabled true; LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace true; UISupportedInterfaceOrientations [UIInterfaceOrientationPortrait]; UILaunchScreen {}; CFBundleDocumentTypes + UTExportedTypeDeclarations for com.shreehub.mapper.project conforming to com.apple.package and public.content with extension mapperproj and LSTypeIsPackage true; ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption false. Add NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription only when a 'Save snapshot to Photos' feature ships. No entitlements file, no UIBackgroundModes for v1.

Runtime gates at launch (all verified declarations): RoomCaptureSession.isSupported, ARWorldTrackingConfiguration.supportsSceneReconstruction(.meshWithClassification), ObjectCaptureSession.isSupported (main actor), PhotogrammetrySession.isSupported, and log os_proc_available_memory(), ProcessInfo.processInfo.physicalMemory, MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice()?.recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize into the app log so build 1 tells you the real memory ceiling on the 13 Pro Max.

Storage layout: Documents/Projects/<uuid>.mapperproj/ { project.json (Codable, schema version), raw/ { worldmap.arworldmap (NSKeyedArchiver), mesh/<anchorUUID>.mchunk (header + packed float3 vertices, float3 normals, uint32 faces, uint8 classification), keyframes/<index>.heic (CIContext.writeHEIFRepresentation, q 0.8), depth/<index>.f16 (Float16 256x192) + <index>.conf (UInt8), poses.json (array of {index, timestamp, transform:[16 Float], intrinsics:[9 Float], imageSize}) , room.capturedroomdata.json (CapturedRoomData is Codable), objects/<id>/Images + Snapshots }, derived/ { textured.usdz, raw_mesh.obj|usdz, clean.usdz (CapturedRoom.export .parametric/.mesh), floorplan.json, floorplan.pdf, measurements.json } }. Mark raw/ isExcludedFromBackup after every write batch; derived/ and project.json stay backed up.

Serialization: JSON via Codable for everything small; a `struct Transform4: Codable { var m: [Float] /* 16, column-major */ }` wrapper with init(_ simd: simd_float4x4) / var simd: simd_float4x4 for poses; raw little-endian binary files with a 16-byte header {magic 'MCHK', version UInt16, count UInt32, stride UInt16} for mesh, depth and confidence. Skip SQLite and binary plist; the data volume is dominated by images and mesh blobs, not records.

Memory strategy: keep only the latest ARMeshAnchor geometry per anchor id in RAM (dictionary keyed by UUID, updated in session(_:didUpdate:)), flush to disk on a serial IO queue, throttle keyframe capture to ~1 fps or on pose delta (>0.3 m or >15 degrees), write depth/keyframes synchronously inside the delegate via copied Data, and feed PhotogrammetrySession with the images directory URL rather than an in-memory sample array. Subscribe to UIApplication.didReceiveMemoryWarningNotification and ProcessInfo.thermalStateDidChangeNotification and pause capture at .serious/.critical thermal state.

Processing runs foregrounded: set UIApplication.shared.isIdleTimerDisabled = true while scanning/processing, show progress from PhotogrammetrySession.outputs (.processingProgress), and persist a resumable checkpointDirectory so a jetsam kill can resume. Add an #available(iOS 26, *) branch using BGContinuedProcessingTaskRequest for the iOS 26 phone later; do not request the GPU resource (entitlement unavailable).

project.yml: keep XcodeGen's SWIFT_VERSION '5.0', set SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY to targeted for useful warnings, TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY '1', IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET 18.0 (nothing in this topic needs 17.0; RoomPlan iOS 17 APIs like init(arSession:) and StructureBuilder are in range), CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED NO for the unsigned CI archive. Render with RealityKit (ARView / RealityView) or Metal, not SceneKit.

Deployment: keep the bundle id stable across weekly re-sideloads so Documents survives; note that only 3 sideloaded apps can coexist with a free ID; document per-device Developer Mode enablement in the runbook; plan the iOS 26 phone install within the 10-App-IDs/7-days and device limits (a second device under the same Apple ID is fine).
open_questions: Exact jetsam ActiveHardMemoryLimit for iPhone 13 Pro Max on iOS 18.3.2 (community reports suggest ~3 GB on 6 GB devices, 2.2-2.3 GB available on 4 GB iPhone 13); must be measured with os_proc_available_memory() on device in build 1.
PhotogrammetrySession.limits.maximumNumberOfInputImages on A15/6 GB devices is undocumented numerically; read at runtime and size keyframe capture for objects accordingly.

Whether Sideloadly's free-team provisioning profile can carry com.apple.developer.kernel.increased-memory-limit (almost certainly not; unverified). If it could, it would be the single biggest lever for photogrammetry headroom.

ARKit depth resolution (256x192) and the 1920x1440 default video format are community/WWDC facts, not present in the doc JSON; confirm from ARCamera.imageResolution and CVPixelBufferGetWidth(depthMap) on device.
Free Apple ID device-UDID limit per 7 days (Corellium says 3) is not stated by Sideloadly or Apple; irrelevant for two phones but worth knowing if a third test device appears.
Whether iOS 26 on the second phone changes any of the above (BGContinuedProcessingTask becomes available; SceneKit deprecation only affects the SDK, not runtime).

unverified_critical_claims: UIRequiredDeviceCapabilities has NO value for LiDAR. The complete value list is: accelerometer, arkit, armv7, arm64, auto-focus-camera, bluetooth-le, camera-flash, driverkit, front-facing-camera, gamekit, gps, gyroscope, healthkit, iphone-performance-gaming-tier, iphone-ipad-minimum-performance-a12, location-services, magnetometer, metal, microphone, nfc, opengles-1/2/3, peer-peer, sms, still-camera, telephony, video-camera, wifi. Use `arkit` (and optionally `metal`, `arm64`) and gate LiDAR at runtime with RoomCaptureSession.isSupported / ARWorldTrackingConfiguration.supportsSceneReconstruction(.mesh).

RoomPlan, ARKit scene reconstruction and RealityKit Object Capture require NO entitlement on iOS. The Entitlements reference lists ARKit entitlements only under 'Enterprise' for visionOS (com.apple.developer.arkit.main-camera-access.allow etc.). The only requirement is NSCameraUsageDescription in Info.plist; the app crashes on first camera access without it.

On iOS, PhotogrammetrySession supports ONLY the .reduced detail level. .preview/.medium/.full/.raw are macOS 12+/Mac Catalyst 15+ only and .custom (CustomDetailSpecification, maximumPolygonCount, texture dims) is macOS 14+ only. .reduced = <50k triangles, ~10 MB, diffuse + AO + normal maps.

SceneKit is deprecated in the iOS 26 SDK: the SceneKit framework, SCNView, SCNScene and ARKit's ARSCNView are all marked deprecated at iOS 26.0 ('Use RealityView instead' / 'SceneKit is deprecated, use RealityKit instead', WWDC25 session 288). They still compile with Xcode 26.6 (warnings only). Model I/O (MDLAsset, MDLMesh, MDLAsset.export(to:), canExportFileExtension(_:)) is NOT deprecated. RealityKit ARView and ModelEntity are not deprecated.

simd_float4x4 is NOT Codable. Its documented conformances are exactly: BitwiseCopyable, Copyable, CustomDebugStringConvertible, Equatable, Escapable, Sendable. A wrapper is required for JSON (e.g. encode columns.0...columns.3 as [Float] of 16 values, column-major) or store poses in a binary blob. simd_float3x3 (ARCamera.intrinsics) likewise needs a wrapper.

Long-running processing cannot be continued in the background on iOS 18. BGContinuedProcessingTask / BGContinuedProcessingTaskRequest (start in foreground, continue in background with a Live Activity) are iOS 26.0+ only. On iOS 18 the options are: (a) beginBackgroundTask(withName:expirationHandler:) which gives 'a limited amount of time' (community: ~30 s) and (b) BGProcessingTask which 'run[s] only when the device is idle' and 'The system terminates any background processing tasks running when the user starts using the device' (needs UIBackgroundModes=processing + BGTaskSchedulerPermittedIdentifiers, registration must complete before applicationDidFinishLaunching ends). Therefore mesh/photogrammetry processing must run while the app is foregrounded; keep the screen awake with UIApplication.shared.isIdleTimerDisabled = true.

Swift 6 language mode is opt-in via SWIFT_VERSION=6 (-swift-version 6). XcodeGen's base setting preset hardcodes SWIFT_VERSION: '5.0' for every generated project, so a project.yml that does not override it compiles in Swift 5 mode with minimal concurrency checking: Sendable/actor-isolation problems are at most warnings and will not fail the CI build. Xcode 26 changes only affect NEW Xcode templates (Default Actor Isolation = MainActor); XcodeGen projects get the 'existing project' defaults (SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION unset = nonisolated, SWIFT_APPROACHABLE_CONCURRENCY unset = NO).

Free Apple ID sideloading limits (Sideloadly FAQ): 'a free Apple Developer account is limited to 3 sideloaded apps' installed at once; 'only allows the app to function for 7 days' then re-sideload with the same Apple ID; 'You may create up to 10 App IDs every 7 days'; 'Since iOS 16+, Apple now requires users to enable Developer Mode'. Developer Mode is a per-device switch (Settings > Privacy & Security > Developer Mode, requires restart) and the toggle only appears after the device has been paired/had an install attempted.
